insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Day Care Procedures
great.quote: g) All day care procedures are covered.
great.explanation: Day care treatments that do not require 24-hour hospitalization are covered. This means you can claim for many minor procedures without needing full hospital admission.

great.name: Hospice Care
great.quote: Hospice Care : Payable up to 20% of sum insured at network providers on indemnity basis, payable once in life time. Available after a waiting period of 12 months from the policy inception.
great.explanation: Hospice care is covered once in a lifetime up to 20% of the sum insured after a 12-month waiting period. This provides early specialized support for end-of-life care at network hospitals.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: a) Room (Single Standard A/c), Boarding, Nursing expenses as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home.
good.explanation: Room rent is for a Single Standard AC room, which is a common standard in many health plans. This means you get a private room but not the highest category.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days except accidents. This is a standard waiting period protecting against immediate claims.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Exclusions, Code Excl 02 (Specified disease / procedure waiting period)
good.explanation: A 24-month waiting period applies for listed specific diseases and procedures. This is a typical duration before these conditions are covered.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry 30 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer.
good.reference: PED exclusion text shown in document (under exclusions section content near modern treatment table)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 30 months of continuous coverage. This is within the acceptable range of 24 to 48 months.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: e) Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This standard duration helps cover diagnostic and preparatory tests.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: f) Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital. The amount payable shall be up to 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization.
good.explanation: Expenses up to 60 days after discharge are covered, which is standard. However, note the payout cap mentioned separately.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: Cumulative bonus calculated at 5% of basic sum insured for each claim free year subject to a maximum of 50% of the basic sum insured... In the event of a claim... such cumulative bonus so granted will be reduced at the same rate at which it has accrued
good.explanation: No claim bonus grows by 5% per claim-free year up to 50%, but reduces proportionally after a claim. This is a standard bonus structure.

good.name: AYUSH Treatment
good.quote: AYUSH Treatment: Medical expenses for Inpatient Hospitalization incurred on treatment under Ayurveda, Unani, Sidha and Homeopathy systems of medicines in a AYUSH Hospital is payable up to the sum insured. Note : Claims under Yoga and Naturopathy system of treatment will be payable subject to prior approval from the company.
good.explanation: Inpatient AYUSH treatments are covered up to the sum insured, with Yoga and Naturopathy needing prior approval. This aligns with common AYUSH coverage.

good.name: Optional Cover
good.quote: Section  II  Lumpsum Cover for Cancer (Optional Cover Available only if speciﬁcally opted on payment of additional premium and shown in the policy schedule)... A waiting period of 30 months is applicable for this lump-sum beneﬁt cover
good.explanation: An optional lump-sum cancer cover is available after a 30-month waiting period. This is an add-on benefit beyond the base indemnity cover.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern treatment... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below.
bad.explanation: Modern treatments have explicit monetary sub-limits, which can increase your out-of-pocket expenses for advanced procedures.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Cataract treatment: The company will pay the expenses incurred for treatment of cataract up to the limits mentioned below; ... 5,00,000/- 30,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 40,000/- per person per policy period ... 7,50,000/- and 10,00,000/- 40,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 60,000/- per person per policy period
bad.reference: Section I (h) and cataract limit table
bad.explanation: Cataract treatment has fixed monetary caps per eye and per policy period, which may be restrictive depending on actual treatment costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Hospitalisation expenses which vary based on the room occupied by the insured person will be considered in proportion to the room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section I (a) Note; also aligns with 'Associated Medical Expenses' definition
bad.explanation: If you choose a room higher than the eligible Single Standard AC, claim amounts for related expenses will be proportionately reduced, lowering your payout.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization Cap
bad.quote: The amount payable shall be up to 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization.
bad.explanation: Although post-hospitalization expenses are covered for 60 days, the payout is capped at 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization, which may limit claim amounts.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: Not mentioned in the provided policy wording text.
bad.reference: Document review: no restore/reinstatement/recharge clause found in provided pages
bad.explanation: There is no mention of a restore or recharge benefit, so once the sum insured is exhausted, it is not replenished during the policy year.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Not mentioned in the coverage as 'consumables covered' or any consumables add-on/benefit.
bad.reference: Section I coverage list (a)-(p) does not state consumables are covered separately
bad.explanation: Consumables like gloves, syringes, and PPE are not explicitly covered, so you may have to pay for these separately if billed by the hospital.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Copayment : This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.explanation: A 10% co-pay applies only for entry age 61 and above. This is a common senior-age co-pay and does not affect younger insured persons.

bad.name: Co-pay Applicability
bad.quote: Copayment : This policy is subject to co-payment of 10%... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.explanation: Co-pay is clearly stated for entry age 61+, but the policy does not explicitly confirm if co-pay is zero for younger ages. Clarification from insurer or schedule is needed.

unclear.name: NCB Reduction
unclear.quote: In the event of a claim resulting in... the cumulative bonus so granted will be reduced at the same rate at which it has accrued... Full utilization of Basic Sum Insured and full utilization of cumulative bonus accrued, the cumulative bonus on renewal will be “nil”
unclear.explanation: The policy states that cumulative bonus reduces proportionally after claims, but exact details on how small claims affect bonus and calculation examples are not provided.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
